newsitem.title: USA: MCI seeks sanctions on Nynex.
newsitem.headline: MCI seeks sanctions on Nynex.

text.p: MCI Communications Corp. said Tuesday it asked New York state regulators to impose sanctions on Nynex Corp. for refusing to sign an agreement that would have provided final terms for MCI to offer local phone service in the state.
The two companies had agreed on most of the terms for governing local competition after more than a year of negotiations and litigation, Washington-based MCI said.
Both parties had agreed the remaining issues would be brought before the state Public Service Commission for a final decision within 10 days.
Washington-based MCI said Nynex instead filed a new version of the agreement with the commission that neither the panel nor MCI had seen, in an attempt to delay competition in local phone service.

Nynex said it welcomes competition, and that it is in the company's interest to reach an interconnection agreement with MCI in order to become a long-distance provider, but that it would not sign an agreement "at any price."
A Nynex spokesman could not immediately provide details about the differences between the two agreements, nor could he say when the Nynex version of the contract would be available to be seen by MCI.
But Nynex said MCI had mischaracterized the nature of the dispute. "We could just as easily ask why they did not sign our version of the interconnect agreement," said the spokesman.

MCI has requested the commission approve the contract as previously agreed upon, including MCI's version of the disputed contract sections, and order sanctions against Nynex, including attorneys' fees for bad faith, 11th-hour tactics.
